# jasy

> Declarative, component-based PDF generation in pure TypeScript, inspired by Flutter's widget tree. ZUGFeRD / XRechnung / Factur-X e-invoices are built in. No headless browser, no Java - the low-level PDF byte stream is hand-written, and text is laid out with real font metrics, so word-wrapping and pagination are computed, not guessed. It renders in Node and in the browser.

jasy (npm scope `@jasy`, MIT, by Florian Heuberger) lets you describe a document as a tree of components - `Document`, `Page`, `Column`, `Row`, `Box`, `Text`, `Paragraph`, `Image`, `Svg`, `Canvas`, `Table`, `Positioned`, `Flow`, form fields and more - and renders it to a PDF. Text styles cascade like CSS/Flutter, content paginates correctly across pages (repeating table headers, headers and footers, newspaper columns), and TrueType/WOFF fonts embed subsetted. The same documents can be authored as Vue components (`@jasy/vue`, `@jasy/nuxt`) or React components (`@jasy/react`).

Install: `pnpm add @jasy/pdf`. Minimal example:

```ts
import { Document, Page, Text, renderToBytes } from "@jasy/pdf";
const doc = Document([Page([Text("Hello PDF", { size: 24, bold: true })])]);
const bytes = await renderToBytes(doc);
```

The same in React:

```tsx
import { Document, Page, Text, renderToPdf } from "@jasy/react";
const bytes = await renderToPdf(
  <Document>
    <Page>
      <Text size={24} bold>Hello PDF</Text>
    </Page>
  </Document>,
);
```

The strategic focus is **e-invoicing**: `@jasy/e-invoice` turns a typed `Invoice` into a conformant **PDF/A-3 with embedded EN-16931 CII/UBL XML**, checked with the official KoSIT EN-16931 + XRechnung Schematron and veraPDF (PDF/A). It is the dependency-light Node answer to Java's Mustangproject, PHP's horstoeko/zugferd and Python's factur-x.

## Docs

- [PDF engine](https://jasy.dev/docs/pdf): layout, text, tables, images, fonts, pages, columns, positioning, encryption, emoji, accessibility, rotation, navigation, drawing, forms, output
- [PDFs in Vue](https://jasy.dev/docs/vue): author documents as Vue components, rendered in the browser or on a server
- [PDFs in Nuxt](https://jasy.dev/docs/nuxt): the zero-config Nuxt module, client or server
- [PDFs in React](https://jasy.dev/docs/react): author documents as React components, rendered in the browser or on a server
- [E-invoicing](https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing): the Invoice model, ZUGFeRD/XRechnung profiles, validation, a complete example, your own layout
- [CLI](https://jasy.dev/docs/cli): the `jasy` terminal tool to read, validate and export ZUGFeRD / XRechnung e-invoices

## Packages

- [@jasy/pdf](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/pdf): the core declarative PDF engine
- [@jasy/vue](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/vue): PDFs as Vue components
- [@jasy/nuxt](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/nuxt): the Nuxt module
- [@jasy/react](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/react): PDFs as React components
- [@jasy/e-invoice](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/e-invoice): ZUGFeRD / Factur-X / XRechnung e-invoices (PDF/A-3 + EN-16931 XML)
- [@jasy/cli](https://npmx.dev/package/@jasy/cli): the command-line tool (binary `jasy`)

## Links

- [Showroom](https://jasy.dev/showroom): live code on the left, the exact rendered PDF on the right - sixteen real templates
- [Benchmark](https://jasy.dev/benchmark): six documents, four engines, every comparison held to the same text on the same pages
- [Validator](https://jasy.dev/validate): check any ZUGFeRD or XRechnung PDF (made by any tool) against veraPDF + the official EN-16931 rules
- [GitHub](https://github.com/jasy-pdf/jasy): source, MIT licensed
